:::{#sol-sum-intersection-subspace-practice}

A vector of $\mathcal{S}_2$ is $s\,(1, 1, 0) + t\,(0, 0, 1) = (s, s, t)$.
It is in $\mathcal{S}_1$
exactly when its third entry is $0$,
that is, when $t = 0$.
So

$$
\mathcal{S}_1 \cap \mathcal{S}_2 = \cb{(s, s, 0) : s \in \reals} = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 1, 0)},
$$

a line through the origin, which is a [subspace](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-subspace),
as @thm-sum-intersection-subspace says.

:::
